channel.title: Signal & Noise Private
channel.description: Signal & Noise is a personal podcast made for Augusto Restrepo. Each episode takes a topic he's been following — articles, posts, research and conversations he curates from across the web — and double-clicks on it. Max, the optimist, makes the bull case; Lena, the skeptic, pokes holes in it. Together they separate the signal from the noise, so the big ideas are easier to understand and judge. Casual, curious, and grounded in facts.

item.title: Thesis Check: AI Infrastructure — Five greens, three yellows underneath — Max vs Lena
item.description:
Weekly Thesis Check #2: AI Infrastructure (Broadcom, Taiwan Semi, Nvidia, EWY, ARTY), covering news from about Sep 6 to Oct 4, 2026. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) walk each ticker's price path and C1/C2/C3 stop-lights. Scoreboard stays five overall greens; three criteria underneath are yellow (Broadcom operating-margin trend, Nvidia gross-margin guide, EWY memory-price momentum). Buy-rules v3 one-liner: Taiwan Semi and Arty BUY; Broadcom, Nvidia, and EWY HOLD.
Chapters: Open; Broadcom; Taiwan Semi; Nvidia; EWY; Arty; Close.
Made-up call-ins, invented for this episode: Priya, a fictional Bangalore semiconductor supply-chain analyst; Callum, a fictional Glasgow memory-markets desk analyst.
Sources: Augusto's thesis tracker (scores as of the Oct 2 tracker file), Robinhood market data (quotes, historicals, analyst ratings, earnings calendar as of Oct 2–4), company IR (Broadcom FQ3, TSMC monthly revenue and Q3 calendar, Nvidia Q2 commentary), TrendForce memory PRs (Sep 7/29/30), Reuters/CNBC on the Sep 14 AI-safety selloff, Reuters on the Broadcom–Anthropic financing report (Oct 1), iShares ARTY product page, and the 10am.pro group chat (paraphrased). Earnings dates marked company-verified where Robinhood says so; otherwise tentative. Stop-light changes are suggestions only; the tracker is unchanged. Numbers rounded. Not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. Five greens, three yellows underneath; 2. Broadcom — green with a soft margin; 3. Taiwan Semi — all green into October fifteenth; 4. Nvidia — beat-and-raise, softer gross margin; 5. E-W-Y — memory still rising, just slower; 6. Arty — base layer still healthy; 7. Healthy picks and shovels, watch the yellows.

item.title: Thesis Episode 0.5: The Buy Rules — Max vs Lena
item.description:
Thesis Episode 0.5, take two: Augusto's new buy rules (version 3, locked Oct 3, 2026), explained from scratch. This replaces the earlier Episode 0.5, which was built on Friday's draft timing light. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) cover why the rules changed (what the stress test, the red-team and the full 22-position backtest found), then the eight rules in plain words: "add-worthy" means a green thesis with all three criteria green; above the 200-day simple moving average you buy, below it you re-check the thesis first; crypto and speculative names have a hard floor and wait in SGOV; new listings get a half ticket; the rules never sell; ticket size and caps are still to be decided; and there's no earnings blackout, just no resting limit orders through a report. They also go over what was cut from the draft (the seven checks, RSI, volume breakouts, tiers, event blackouts), what survived from Hernán's (10AMPRO) method, a worked example board from Friday's close, and how the weekly Thesis Check episodes will mention it.
Made-up call-ins, invented for this episode: Hank, a fictional Chicago quant, and Tess, a fictional San Francisco fundamental analyst.
Sources: the Investment advisor's locked buy rules v3 (Oct 3, 2026) and the evidence files behind them (full-book backtest, v3 red-team, stress test of v2), plus the advisor's notes on Hernán's method. The worked examples use tracker lights as scored Oct 1-2 (before any v3 re-score) and our own check of Friday's closes against the simple 200-day average; they aren't the advisor's official dashboard. Not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. Take two; 2. Why the rules changed; 3. Rule one: add-worthy; 4. Rules two and three: the line; 5. Call-in: Hank and the backtests; 6. The exceptions, and the never-sell rule; 7. What got cut, and what came from Hernán; 8. Call-in: Tess on the re-check; 9. Friday's board; 10. Still open, and how we'll use it.

item.title: All-In This Week: White House AI Accord — Max vs Lena
item.description:
An unofficial recap of the past week of the All-In podcast (Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks and David Friedberg), Sep 30–Oct 2, 2026. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go topic by topic through both episodes released after last week's Daniel Ek interview: the Summit interview "Jake Paul & The Chainsmokers: Turning Fame into Funds, Jake Enters Politics? & Venture Bubble Signs" (Sep 30), and the main show, episode 291, "Trump's Super Intelligence Summit, AI Safety Accord, GDP Beats, Midterm Predictions" (Oct 2).
Topics: the White House Super Intelligence Summit and voluntary AI safety accord (six frontier labs, external audits, board fiduciary duty, D&O teeth); cybersecurity arms race and data centers as national security; America.gov and coordinated "doomer" messaging; GDP/jobs/inflation beats versus diesel, rates and a late-October bank-impairment warning; midterm and 2028 predictions; media coverage of the attempted Dubai–Tel Aviv hijacking; Jake Paul's attention-as-capital thesis, MVP vs UFC, and politics ambitions; The Chainsmokers on music-to-venture, sixth-man investing, DPI and bubble tells.
Made-up guests: Mara, a fictional Vancouver AI governance lawyer, joins in the Accord chapter. Finn, a fictional Auckland creator-economy investor, joins in the Jake Paul chapter. Both are invented for this episode and speak for no real firm.
Sources: the official All-In episode descriptions and timestamps (Apple Podcasts / iTunes lookup), and published episode transcripts (Podscripts) for both episodes, cross-checked against a public write-up of episode 291. Hosts only describe what the besties said, and they don't imitate their voices. Where a transcript didn't make clear who said something, we say "one of them". Numbers are rounded and are the speakers' claims unless we say otherwise. This is not affiliated with All-In and is not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. This week on All-In; 2. The White House Accord; 3. Cyber arms race and data centers; 4. America.gov and the doomer war; 5. GDP beats and the rate problem; 6. Midterms and 2028; 7. The Dubai flight and the media; 8. Jake Paul and attention as capital; 9. Chainsmokers, sixth men, and bubble tells; 10. What we'd watch next.

item.title: Thesis Episode Zero: The Map — Max vs Lena
item.description:
Episode zero of the Thesis Check series: the map. A from-scratch tour of Augusto's whole investment-thesis framework for a smart listener who's new to it. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) cover every bucket (Ballast, Legacy Colombia, AI Verticals, AI Infrastructure, Musk, Apple, Electricity, and the new Crypto lines: Bitcoin, the on-chain engine with Solana and XRP, and a small speculative bet), each with its core idea, its tickers and its rough weight as a share of the portfolio. They also explain how the follow-up works: the C1/C2/C3 stop lights with the starred anchor, the overall-light logic, kill-committee memos, hold-and-harvest, quarterly re-scores and the weekly rotation. Current scoreboard: 17 green, 3 yellow, 2 red.
Made-up call-ins, invented for this episode: Rosalind, a fictional East Coast private-wealth advisor, and Sipho, a fictional Cape Town on-chain analyst.
Sources: Augusto's thesis tracker and crypto thresholds (both updated Oct 1, 2026) and the Tesis & Exits master map v0.6 (bucket weights are a mid-September snapshot, rounded). Not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. Episode zero: the map; 2. How the stop lights work; 3. Ballast and Legacy Colombia; 4. AI Verticals; 5. AI Infrastructure; 6. Musk; 7. Apple: hold and harvest; 8. Electricity; 9. Crypto: the new lines; 10. Scoreboard and wrap-up.

item.title: All-In This Week: Anthropic's IPO Wobble and the Open-Source Flood — Max vs Lena
item.description:
An unofficial recap of the past week of the All-In podcast (Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks and David Friedberg), Sep 21–29, 2026. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go topic by topic through all six episodes released that week: the main show, episode 290 ("Anthropic IPO at Risk, Meta's Muse Pop, Token Prices Fall, Open Source Gains Share, Alignment Fails", Sep 25), plus the Summit and interview episodes with Naveen Rao (Sep 21), Blake Scholl (Sep 22), Steve Hilton & Spencer Pratt (Sep 22), Luca Ferrari (Sep 23) and Daniel Ek (Sep 28).
Topics: "labs" vs. companies and product liability; the flood of open-weight models and the claimed flip in token share; whether Anthropic's IPO is in trouble (Polymarket odds, super-voting shares, Chamath's "$1 trillion or less" math, Sacks' "stable duopoly on a hamster wheel"); Bernie Sanders' superintelligence bill, Trump, Bessent and Obama; Meta's Muse, agents and the App Store's 30% cut; alignment, Claude's constitution and Anthropic's wet lab; AI's energy wall (Naveen Rao's dynamical computer, Boom's jet engines for data centers); Bending Spoons' buy-and-fix model; California's governor race; and Daniel Ek's $499 Neko Health scan.
Made-up guest: Dev, a fictional quant, joins briefly in the Anthropic chapter. He is invented for this episode and speaks for no real fund.
Sources: the official All-In episode descriptions and timestamps (RSS feed and YouTube), published episode transcripts (Happy Scribe) for five episodes, and our own Whisper transcription of the Daniel Ek episode's audio, cross-checked against published summaries. Hosts only describe what the besties said, and they don't imitate their voices. Where a transcript didn't make clear who said something, we say "one of them". Numbers are rounded and are the speakers' claims (for example valuations, Polymarket odds, token-share charts and company stats) unless we say otherwise. This is not affiliated with All-In and is not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. This week on All-In; 2. They're not labs, they're companies; 3. The open-source flood; 4. Is Anthropic's IPO in trouble?; 5. Bernie, Trump, Obama and the politics of AI; 6. Muse, agents and the App Store's thirty percent; 7. Alignment, Claude's constitution and the wet lab; 8. The energy wall: Naveen Rao and Boom's jet engines; 9. Bending Spoons: buying product-market fit; 10. California: Steve Hilton and Spencer Pratt; 11. Daniel Ek, Neko and the body scan; 12. What we'd watch next.

item.title: NAUT: Can You Read Your Way to a 10x? — Max vs Lena (Special)
item.description:
A one-off special. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) dig into Nautilus Biotechnology (NAUT), the Seattle proteomics company the 10am.pro group has been debating as the "read" layer of the biology-is-code thesis, on a day the stock jumped about 30% with no company news we could find. They cover what proteoforms are and why they matter, the September Nature Methods tau paper, the July pivot from Broadscale to proteoform assays (tau first, then AKT1 in oncology, roughly 20 assays targeted by mid-2028), and the money: about $130M in cash, roughly $14M of quarterly burn, a raise expected before mid-2027 and a new $125M at-the-market program. They also run NAUT through the lessons from Lucas's LLM 10x stock contest and his "Linares lens" chart. A made-up guest, Bev (a fictional retired lab-instrument saleswoman), asks who actually buys a roughly $1M machine.
Sources: the 10am.pro group discussion; Lucas's LLM 10x Stock Contest PDFs and Linares-lens chart; the proteomics paper shared in the group (Cell Reports Medicine spotlight on a Nature Medicine plasma-proteome aging-clock study); Hernán's "Biology is Code" page (mercados.10am.pro/biology-is-code); Antonio Linares, "Nautilus: Tesla for Proteomics" (Sep 28, 2026); Nautilus Q2 2026 results and earnings call, the Sep 4 Nature Methods release and the Sep 11 8-K; prices as of mid-afternoon Sep 29, 2026. Numbers are rounded, and company claims are flagged as such. Bev is fictional. This is not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. Thirty percent before lunch; 2. Why proteins, why now; 3. The pivot nobody clapped for; 4. Bev sells the machine; 5. Cash, burn, and the at-the-market button; 6. Through Lucas's lenses; 7. Revolution, option, or lottery ticket.

item.title: Biology Eats the Market — Max vs Lena (Special)
item.description:
A one-off special. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) debate Antonio Linares's "bio/acc basket": his claim that biology drives most market returns over the next decade, and his four picks. Nautilus (NAUT) reads the proteome, Recursion (RXRX) designs drugs with A.I., ImmunityBio (IBRX) reboots the immune system with Anktiva, and MiNK Therapeutics (INKT) takes iNKT cell therapy after solid tumors. Max makes the case from the post and its 33-minute video: biology becomes code, a read, design, reboot and strike stack, disciplined management teams, and pharma money already flowing into Recursion. Lena pushes back with the latest filings: Nautilus's first revenue of about $0.2M and its Broadscale delay, Recursion's cash burn, ImmunityBio's 45x sales valuation and the FDA warning letter, and MiNK's roughly $9M cash plus a 17-patient phase 2 with zero responses. A made-up guest, Nigel, drops by to heckle the whole idea of "platform" biotech.
Source (credit): Antonio Linares (@alc2022) on X, Sep 28, 2026, https://x.com/alc2022/status/2104620231922745534 (post and attached video). Also referenced: Q2 2026 results and filings from Nautilus, Recursion, ImmunityBio and MiNK; ImmunityBio's FDA warning letter and PDUFA date; MiNK's AACR 2026 phase 2 poster; market prices as of the Sep 28, 2026 close. Numbers are rounded. The hosts flag claims they couldn't verify on air. Nigel is fictional. This is not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. Biology is the new compute; 2. Read it, then design it; 3. Reboot and strike; 4. A stack or four lottery tickets?.

item.title: HIMS Isn't Telemedicine — Max vs Lena (Special)
item.description:
A one-off special. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) talk through "HIMS No Es Telemedicina", a Substack piece by Hernán Jaramillo and Antonio Linares of 10ampro. The piece argues that the market prices HIMS like a call center that hands out prescriptions, and that this is a category error. Its case rests on Linares's "closed loop" idea, with Spotify and Duolingo as comparisons: intake, treatment, follow-up and outcome, all owned by one company. Lena pushes back on the customer-service horror story, the FTC case (including the health-data sharing allegations the article leaves out), acquired versus organic growth, competition from Novo, Amazon and OpenAI, and the empty "sold with margin" box: negative free cash flow and a shrinking gross margin.
Source article (credit): Hernán Jaramillo & Antonio Linares, "HIMS No Es Telemedicina", 10ampro on Substack, Sep 27, 2026, https://substack.com/home/post/p-217692613. The framework comes from Antonio Linares's "The State of the Ontology Velocity" (Sep 15, 2026). Also referenced: the Hims & Hers Q2 2026 results and earnings call (Aug 10, 2026), the FTC complaint and press release (Jul 29, 2026), Teladoc's Q2 2026 results, and public HIMS price data as of the Sep 25, 2026 close. Numbers are rounded. Claims the hosts couldn't verify are flagged on air. This is not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. The double charge; 2. Loop, not data; 3. Teladoc's graveyard and the four links; 4. The FTC and the anecdote; 5. Who copies it, and the empty box.
